subjects.displayTitle: Spiritual assemblies: authority expressed through service
subjects.introduction: Those who hold real authority, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says, are known by their humility and self-sacrifice and show no air of superiority over their friends. That is a strange way to describe an institution, and it is the clue to what a spiritual assembly is for. Bahá’u’lláh ordains that in every city a house be raised in the name of justice, whose members should feel they are entering the presence of God and should weigh the interests of others as carefully as their own. The work itself is unglamorous and concrete: schooling for girls and boys, care for orphans and the widows of martyrs, funds guarded and accounted for, letters answered, disputes settled with kindness. Members are chosen by election, young or old, rich or poor, and once a decision is reached everyone supports it, though frank expression beforehand is a sacred obligation. The early church’s choice of trusted people to look after neglected widows shows another community discovering that service must be organised to be real [1]. The way forward runs through the art of consultation, the spirit in which elections are held, and the building of a community whose vitality is the truest measure of its institutions.
subjects.arc: Begin with humility and the meaning of an assembly, follow its purposes and practical service, examine elections and consultation in their historical settings, then read the later guidance on mutual trust and institutional maturity.

order.why: Connect collective institutions with unity and harmony.
shortened: The Spiritual Assemblies are collectively the most effective of all instruments for establishing unity and harmony. This matter is of the utmost importance; this is the magnet that draweth down the confirmations of God.

order.why: Open with humility as the sign of real authority.
shortened: The ones in real authority are known by their humility and self-sacrifice and show no attitude of superiority over the friends.

order.why: Explore the source’s definition of a spiritual assembly.
shortened: O ye blessed souls! Many assemblies are formed and organized in this world but the name of this Assembly is the hope of the people of Heart. It is indicative of teaching and from the Kingdom of Abha is honored with the eloquent Firman.

"Assembly" means the diffusion of the Fragrances of God. "Assembly" means humility and friendliness toward the believers of God. "Assembly" means the promotion of the Word of God. "Assembly" means to be satisfied and holy from all else save God.
Such is the spiritual Assembly. Such is the divine meeting. Such is the lordly congregation!

order.why: Read peace, human oneness, and investigation as purposes.
Consider the images of lamps and gardens.
shortened: These Spiritual Assemblies are aided by the Spirit of God. Their defender is 'Abdu'l‑Baha. Over them He spreadeth His wings. What bounty is there greater than this? These Spiritual Assemblies are shining lamps and heavenly gardens, from which the fragrances of holiness are diffused over all regions, and the lights of knowledge are shed abroad over all created things. From them the spirit of life streameth in every direction. They, indeed, are the potent sources of the progress of man, at all times and under all conditions.

order.why: Read the house established in the name of justice.
shortened: Addressing the nations, the Ancient Beauty ordaineth that in every city in the world a house be established in the name of justice wherein shall gather pure and steadfast souls to the number of the Most Great Name. At this meeting they should feel as if they were entering the Presence of God, inasmuch as this binding command hath flowed from the Pen of Him Who is the Ancient of Days. The glances of God are directed towards this Assembly.

order.why: Consider order as relations inherent in reality.
shortened: O thou organizer of spiritual souls!

The Divine Law and Organization of the Merciful One is in truth this Sacred and Beneficent Dispensation, and this Manifest and clear Path. For the true Order and Law are those inherent properties and necessary conditions in the realities of things, and the essence of existing realities needs these relations.

order.why: Keep the claim of institutional distinctiveness attributed.
shortened: The Spiritual Assemblies to be established in this Age of God, this holy century, have, it is indisputable, had neither peer nor likeness in the cycles gone before. For those assemblages that wielded power were based on the support of mighty leaders of men, while these Assemblies are based on the support of the Beauty of Abha.

order.why: Turn toward qualities members must acquire.
Read the qualities of elected members in the Secret of Divine Civilization’s context.
Keep the related reported formulation of qualifications.
Read election across differences of age and wealth.
shortened: As for the members of the Spiritual Assembly, they must be determined by election. The friends should elect whoever they find suitable, whether old or young, whether wealthy or without means.

order.why: Consider an election carried out in fellowship.
Read the reported emphasis on harmony, education, and character.
shortened: "As to the House of Spirituality the first question related to its election. The election should be carried out with sincerity and good will. People should be elected who when united together will give the most harmony. No one should be electe who would cause inharmony.
Members should be elected who are experienced in the Cause and sufficiently educated. Their character must be good.

order.why: Keep the reported question about qualifications with its reply.
shortened: I asked ‘Abdul Baha what are the qualifications necessary for the members of the Spiritual Meeting. He replied: "They must be souls well known as Baha'is, firm and steadfast in the Covenant.

order.why: Read the reported language of spiritual democracy in its setting.
shortened: There are no offices in this Cause. I do not and have not 'appointed' any one to perform any special services but I encourage everyone to engage in the services of the Kingdom. The foundation of this Cause is pure, spiritual democracy and not a theocracy.

order.why: Consider the reported description of cooperative servants.
Ask what gives an assembly of service its meaning.
shortened: The Assembly of Service is in truth a name with meaning, not a meaningless title. The proof of this is that it spreads the verses of the All-Loving Lord and raises the banners of the Lord of Hosts.

order.why: Begin practical service with care for martyrs’ survivors.
shortened: Regarding the Spiritual Assembly of Yazd, you had written that praise be to God, it has been formed with utmost enthusiasm and the respected members gather on designated days and strive for the comfort of the martyrs' survivors and the protection and preservation of the friends and the management of affairs.

order.why: Read the responsibility for girls’ and boys’ schooling.
shortened: But in these days, this duty is obligatory and essential for the Spiritual Assembly. Therefore, strive as much as you can to establish two schools, for boys and girls, in the utmost order and organization, so that God willing, there will be no need for other schools, and in a short time the children will receive such a Baha'i education that each one will become a shining lamp.

order.why: Keep the reported duties of teaching, education, science, and art.
shortened: In every center where Bahais are sufficiently numerous, a spiritual assembly should be established, to guide and co-ordinate the activities of the friends in the district. The main duties of the Spiritual Assemblies are as follows.

To make arrangements for spreading the Teachings among the people by means of meetings (at which non-believers are welcome) held several times a week, to teach and guide people and to attract and strengthen new Bahais. Next to promote education, science and art. (the spiritual assembly should make itself responsible to see that every child of a Bahai receives a good education.)

order.why: Read care for children, orphans, and incapacitated people.
Examine the protection of entrusted funds.
Consider collective oversight of income and expenditure.
Keep the particular arrangement for contributions.
shortened: However, the arrangement of these contributions is up to the assembly, that is, the honored Afnan of the Blessed Tree Jenab-i-Aqa Siyyid Mehdi, Jenab-i-Afshar, Jenab-i-Haji Siyyid Kazim, Jenab-i-Aqa Mirza Yusuf and others - whatever they deem advisable should be carried out.

order.why: Read kindness and justice in a property matter.
shortened: Regarding the properties you wrote about, refer to the Spiritual Assembly. They will certainly exercise the utmost kindness, justice and grace in your case, and this letter alone is sufficient.

order.why: Retain the particular land dispute and request for clarification.
shortened: O herald of the Covenant and Hand of the Cause of God!

Your letter from Merv was noted and brought the utmost joy. The building plan is most acceptable and desirable - let them build it accordingly. Your honor should temporarily proceed to Tehran due to the matter of the purchased land, as someone has claimed it was a conditional sale. Some of the prominent figures and trustees are seeking information and clarification - you should meet with them as well since this work can be accomplished through you.

order.why: Consider consent before copying recipients’ Tablets.
Read the requirement for trustworthy signed documents.
Distinguish shared deliberative information from an individual’s confidence.
Follow the varied responsibilities of service and correspondence.
shortened: The exaltation of the Word of God and diffusion of the divine fragrances in all parts of the world is obligatory, management of internal and external affairs necessary, caring for the friends and conducting their affairs among the duties, correspondence with all lands and responses to questions continuous and successive.

order.why: Keep the reported duty to attend to community affairs.
shortened: "Their fifth duty is to correct and manage the affairs of the friends and attend to other matters concerning the Cause."

order.why: Read assistance to a traveler as joyful service.
shortened: It was written to Aqa Shaykh 'Ali-Akbar that purely for teaching and diffusing the divine fragrances, he should travel to Gilan, Mazandaran, Tehran, Kashan, Isfahan, Shiraz and the ports of Fars. And arrangements were made for his travel to such a degree that if possible, the Spiritual Assembly should also provide some assistance to him in this regard, and if it is not possible, then so be it. The purpose is that the Spiritual Assembly should serve the friends with the utmost spirit and joy.

order.why: Consider support for the women’s teaching assembly.
shortened: Therefore, utmost importance must be given to the women's teaching assembly so that, through the grace, protection and support of the Most Glorious Beauty (may my spirit be sacrificed for His loved ones), the first women's teaching assembly will be established in Tehran and spread to other regions. This matter is important. The Spiritual Assembly must certainly exert its utmost effort in this matter.

order.why: Read cooperation in the East-West Unity Association.
shortened: O spiritual friends of 'Abdu'l-Baha!

Jinab-i-Mirza Ahmad Sohrab has written a letter from America requesting that individuals be selected to serve as members of the executive committee of the East-West Unity Association, and the letter is being sent enclosed herewith for your review. Therefore, select individuals in Tehran to be named as members of this executive committee, and likewise send copies of this letter along with copies of Jinab-i-Mirza Ahmad's letter to other Assemblies in surrounding areas so that each Assembly may select five people.

order.why: Join assembly, school, and pilgrim house in a particular plan.
Read truthfulness and goodwill toward government and people.
Consider the stated primary purpose of establishing assemblies.
Keep the charge to establish an assembly and share the teachings.
shortened: It is incumbent on thee to organize a spiritual assembly in that city, wherein the mysteries of the Kingdom of thy Lord be spread and this wondrous Manifestation promulgated.

order.why: Hear the appeal for spiritual inspiration.
Read gratitude expressed through fulfilling duties.
Examine the warning about committees becoming names without significance.
shortened: Today all the believers of God must think of conveying the message, and not of the formation of committees; for there will be no result from the organization of the committees. It will be a name without significance. A few days they gather together and then they will be dispersed.

order.why: Keep the particular counsel to leave establishment to the local believers.
Read timing in the response about Oriental delegates.
Consider the importance of the early stages of organization.
Read the news of a proposed general election in Tehran.
Preserve the particular two-stage electoral arrangement.
shortened: Every group, that is every hundred or fifty people, should elect one person, whoever they wish, and these elected individuals will elect the members of the Spiritual Assembly. Whether in the first election or the second election, they should consider the majority. These are the principles of election, that the members of the Spiritual Assembly are the elect of the elected ones.

order.why: Read the explicitly temporary arrangement and its stated circumstances.
shortened: Therefore it appears that the Hands of the Cause, upon them be the Most Glorious Glory of God, and several wise and unbiased friends should gather and name eighty-one distinguished believers. Then divide those souls into groups of nine. Each group of nine should gradually gather in a location and elect one person. Then those nine elected ones should join with the Hands of the Cause to establish a Spiritual Assembly, and all the friends should obey and submit to that Assembly and serve it and strive to uphold its authority.
Thus in that Spiritual Assembly, which is a temporary body until the prescribed assembly is formed, the Hands of the Cause of God are permanent members.

order.why: Keep the historical position of the Hands in that arrangement.
shortened: The Hands of the Cause of God, upon them be the Most Glorious Glory of God, are among the original members and pillars of the Spiritual Assembly and have voting rights.

order.why: Read the nine-or-nineteen provision as specific to Ishqabad’s circumstances.
Consider when a general election would strengthen acceptance.
shortened: O ye beloved friends of 'Abdu'l-Baha! Should you observe that through a general election the Spiritual Assembly will gain increased influence and no one will have cause for objection or hesitation, and all will acknowledge the decisions of the Spiritual Assembly, in such case a general election would be better and more fitting.

order.why: Examine the rejection of multiple votes for influential individuals.
Read the historical provisions for deputies and permission.
Keep the reply referring back to earlier electoral instructions.
Read the reported parliamentary analogy for a convention.
shortened: Are the affairs in the hands of the Assembly of the nations or in the hands of the people? No doubt all affairs are in the hands of the Assembly of the nation, not in the hands of everybody. This Assembly of the Convention is like the Assembly of the nation or Parliament. Those members are [allocated or selected?] by the nation. All affairs are referred to Parliament, not to the people. Parliament discusses affairs and reaches a decision. The Convention is like that and this meeting sees to the affairs and whatever the meeting decided the Executive Board must carry out.

order.why: Retain the related reported explanation of majority decision.
Consider submission to a collective decision.
shortened: The Hands of the Cause of God are like brilliant lamps. Whatever decision they make, or agreement they reach, or majority vote they achieve, all must obey and submit.

order.why: Keep the stated importance and authority of the consultative assembly.
Read the particular instruction concerning the Hands’ decisions.
shortened: It should not be that each person follows their own opinion and thinks independently. When the illustrious Hands of the Cause of God - upon them be the Glory of God - make a decision in any gathering, all must obey and submit, and carry it out with the utmost joy and acceptance, for this obedience is obligatory and necessary.

order.why: Consider organization in relation to the revealed teachings.
Read the point of reference for shared expression.
shortened: And regarding the levels of knowledge and expression, express whatever has issued from this Pen, for everyone is commanded to this, so that all may gather beneath the shade of one word, for the point of reference today is clearly designated.

order.why: Keep the reported caution about relying on spoken accounts.
shortened: Abdul Baha: Whatever anyone thinks he says, but do not trust to what is said unless I have written about it. Whatever I have written with my own hand, that is correct.

order.why: Retain the restored question and answer about daily worship.
Keep the reported speculation about dress in its historical voice.
Consider the concern about competing assemblies in one city.
shortened: Thou hadst asked whether it is permissible to establish two Spiritual Assemblies in one city. Although these assemblies are solely for the purpose of diffusing divine fragrances and promoting the divine teachings, and not Houses of Justice, yet if they become multiple it will cause discord, and from discord a thousand difficulties will appear.

order.why: Hear the response to an assembly in turmoil.
Read the account of members secretly sowing discord.
Return to consultation and harmony.
Keep the instruction to deliberate and decide on a particular letter.
shortened: Read this letter in the Spiritual Assembly and make a definitive decision about this.

order.why: Read the invitation to consult about a practical matter.
shortened: In any case, dear Ustad, if you could arrange for that great plot of land to have all its transactions completely finalized in the government registry - meaning all eight plots would be registered in the name of the Temple, or if eight plots is not possible, then the four middle plots would have their transactions finalized in the government registry in the name of the Temple and we would proceed with constructing the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar - that would be most fitting and would infinitely cause the exaltation of the Cause and the joy of the loved ones of God.
Consult with the Assembly about this matter - perhaps through your efforts this matter will be accomplished, God willing.

order.why: Explains election, consultation and the practical work of spiritual assemblies.
Consider the charitable society’s authority to revise its bylaws.
Read the request to channel affairs during a demanding journey.
shortened: Therefore the Spiritual Assembly must, in whatever way possible, keep affairs flowing in appropriate channels and grant me ample and free respite so that I may complete this perilous journey without distraction of thought and become occupied with that realm.

order.why: Keep the account of repeated correspondence amid many responsibilities.
shortened: Consider then, and be fair: 'Abdu'l-Baha, despite His countless occupations and correspondence with East and West single-handedly, and the attacks of enemies, and the emergence of problems beyond count or measure, has in a short time twice written multiple pages regarding this blessed matter.

order.why: Retain the particular warning about arriving without permission.
Read the appointed visit undertaken on behalf of Abdu’l-Baha.
shortened: On the 28th of Sha'ban, you and four others whom the Spiritual Assembly designates should, like the five planets, journey from the horizon of Tehran to the horizon of Hamadan, and on behalf of 'Abdu'l-Baha visit the pure and goodly resting place of the Name of God.

order.why: Keep the practical question of finding a suitable writer.
Read the choice of the name Spiritual Assembly.
Retain the explanation of House of Spirituality as a group name.
Keep the account of several coordinated assemblies.
shortened: The assemblies are organized and the youth assembly is well-arranged. In truth, the Service Assembly is enthusiastic and desires progress in all affairs of the people. They are obedient to the Spiritual Assembly and revere the Eshkol Assembly.

order.why: Read prayers for the consultative and service assemblies.
Hear the assurance addressed to a devoted assembly.
shortened: O ye who are firm in the Covenant! 'Abdu'l‑Baha is constantly engaged in ideal communication with any Spiritual Assembly which is instituted through the divine bounty, and the members of which, in the utmost devotion, turn to the divine Kingdom and are firm in the Covenant.

order.why: Consider the promise connected with steadfast service.
shortened: This assembly has been formed at a very opportune time. My hope is that it may become a magnet for divine confirmations. If it continues with steadfastness, the assembly will become so brilliant that it will shine like the full moon at the zenith of eternal glory.

order.why: Read firmness through the images of an edifice and rooted tree.
shortened: The honorable members of this new Assembly, which has been formed at Washington, must be in perfect steadfastness, because no edifice, without firmness and erectness, lasts long and no tree, without being firmly rooted, becomes ornamented with leaves and fruits.

order.why: Keep the weekly report’s visible source omission.
shortened: O ye servants of the Threshold of God!
The weekly reports of [...] were received and I was informed of their beautiful meanings which proved firmness and steadfastness in the Cause of God and solidity in the Covenant of God.
Through the favor and providence of the Beauty of trust that Spiritual Gathering will develop day by day and will be reinforced by the strength of God.

order.why: Read joy at an assembly’s establishment.
shortened: The news of the establishment of the Spiritual Assembly in that land brought joy to hearts. It is hoped that that gathering will become a reflection of the realm above and receive a ray from the Supreme Concourse.

order.why: Retain the greeting to an assembly in the Beloved’s homeland.
shortened: O servants of the Sacred Threshold! Your letter was received and caused the utmost joy, for praise be to God, in the homeland of the Beloved of the horizons a Spiritual Assembly has been established and is radiating light.

order.why: Hear the hope for a gathering’s service.
shortened: You have formed a spiritual assembly and engaged in service at the threshold of the All-Merciful. My utmost hope from the Incomparable Lord is that that gathering may become the manifestation of the favors of the All-Bountiful and through unseen confirmations and undoubted assistance become the envy of every assembly.

order.why: Read the response to Shiraz.
shortened: From the glad tidings of the establishment of the Spiritual Assembly of Shiraz, the utmost joy and delight was obtained. I hope it remains firm and steadfast.

order.why: Keep the image of a gathering adorned by its members.
shortened: O ye who are attracted by the divine fragrances! It is understood that a Spiritual Assembly has been adorned with those heavenly souls and a divine gathering has been established in that region.

order.why: Read unity and service in the Bab’s native land.
shortened: O ye servants near to the threshold of the Blessed Beauty, render thanks unto God that in the native land of His Holiness the Exalted One (may my spirit be a sacrifice unto Him) ye have arranged gatherings and sought love and unity, established a Spiritual Assembly and have arisen to serve the divine Threshold.

order.why: Retain the reports of progress in Esslingen and Stuttgart.
Read the prayer for Philadelphia as a heavenly garden.
Consider wisdom and the avoidance of alarm in establishing institutions.
Keep the response to news of a planned assembly.
Read the hope for the House of Spirituality in its own wording.
Hear happiness at the assembly’s progress.
Consider the hope for peace and human unity.
shortened: It is hoped that this new assembly will cause the shining forth of a brilliant light, will raise high the standard of the Covenant, will spread the holy fragrances from the rose garden of the Testament, will promote the unity of the world of humanity, will become the herald of the Most Great Peace, and will cause the exaltation of the Word of God and reveal the mysteries of the Kingdom of God.

order.why: Read the hope for results from the New York Convention.
shortened: Praise be to God, this year the Convention in New York was held with utmost splendor and it is hoped that it will yield beneficial results.

order.why: Connect consultation with inward spiritual development.
shortened: Thus is the Cause of God growing ever more powerful and the assemblies of consultation have been established in the utmost fellowship and love. This servant hath called for a meeting of the Spiritual Assembly therefore in order that it might become the dawning place of the bounty of the All Merciful, that all may become united and in agreement and all men shall strive to establish spiritual perfections in their innermost realities.

order.why: Keep the encouragement to an assembly in an Iranian city.
shortened: Regarding the consultative gathering which has been designated as the Spiritual Assembly, and by which name it should become known, you must surely exert your utmost effort so that the spiritual assembly may shine forth like a divine candle in that ancient Iranian city.

order.why: Read the aspiration to overcome religious and racial prejudice.
shortened: As for the Spiritual Assembly, I pray that God may assist them in all affairs and enable them to exalt the Word of God and promote the divine teachings, so that they may become the cause of human unity and the spread of the divine breaths, until no prejudice remains between religions, denominations and races, and all may hold fast together to the cord of God, and misunderstandings between all parties may vanish, and the human world may become a mirror of the Kingdom of God upon which spiritual lights shine.

order.why: Retain encouragement for the proposed Canadian convention.
shortened: Thou hadst written concerning the convention which thou art going to establish in Canada in the months of September and October. This is highly advisable and I pray God that thou mayest be confirmed and assisted.

order.why: Read recognition of service already offered.
Consider the small Vienna gathering and its hoped-for growth.
shortened: O daughter of the Kingdom! The glad tidings of the establishment of a Baha'i assembly in Vienna have arrived. Although this assembly is now limited to a few souls, yet since it is a divine assembly, like the assembly of the Lord's Supper of Christ, it will expand day by day until it spreads throughout all regions.

order.why: Keep the supplied omissions in the passage joining assemblies and worship.
Reflect on the consequences of action across time.
shortened: Everything produces an impression in existence and results in the course of ages. The (earthly) assemblies established in the different parts of Europe, Asia and America have no results save the help of the physical and the mortal life in this lesser world, for the removal of its conditions and reformation of its customs, and in the end no name will remain thereof. But every spiritual assembly of solid foundation, good structure and unwavering constancy will last forever and will send forth its illumination unto all regions.

order.why: Keep the reported analogy of a center and its surrounding circle.
Read the building materials as an invitation to constructive action.
Close the linked readings with the particular assurance amid loss.
Begin the supplied readings with counsel for the interests of all.
Read the early maturity of local institutions as a process.
Consider the assembly’s many responsibilities to its community.
shortened: Among the more salient objectives to be attained by the local Spiritual Assembly in its process of development to full maturity are to act as a loving shepherd to the Baha'i flock, promote unity and concord among the friends,direct the teaching work, protect the Cause of God, arrange for Feasts, Anniversaries and regular meetings of the community, familiarize the Baha'is with its plans, invite the community to offer its recommendations, promote the welfare of youth and children, and participate, as circumstances permit, in humanitarian activities.

order.why: Examine consultation, informed members, and accountable finances.
shortened: In its own meetings it must endeavor to develop skill in the difficult but highly rewarding art of Baha'i consultation, a process which will require great self-discipline on the part of all members and complete reliance on the power of Baha'u'llah. It should hold regular meetings and ensure that all its members are currently informed of the activities of the assembly, that its Secretary carries out his duties, and its Treasurer holds and disburses the funds of the Faith to its satisfaction, keeping proper accounts and issuing receipts for all contributions.

order.why: Read the wider measures of institutional development.
shortened: ...the Spiritual Assemblies must rise to a new stage in the exercise of their responsibilities as channels of divine guidance, planners of the teaching work, developers of human resources, builders of communities, and loving shepherds of the multitudes.

In sum, the maturity of the Spiritual Assembly must be measured not only by the regularity of its meetings and the efficiency of its functioning, but also by the continuity of the growth of Baha'i membership, the effectiveness of the interaction between the Assembly and the members of its community, the quality of the spiritual and social life of the community, and the overall sense of vitality of a community in the process of dynamic, ever-advancing development.

order.why: Consider seeking advice, help, and protection.
Read the relationship with individuals and families.
Keep the emphasis on teaching.
Read provenance, duties, and loyalty to civil government together.
shortened: As to your query about the Local Spiritual Assembly, it is indeed a divine institution, created by Baha'u'llah in His Kitab-i-Aqdas as the Local House of Justice.

We refer you to the book "Selections from the Writings of 'Abdu'l-Baha", 37, 38, and 40. It is clear that while Local Spiritual Assemblies must supervise all Baha'i matters in their areas, including arrangements for the Nineteen Day Feast, the observance of the Holy Days, the election of the members of the Assembly, promoting the teaching work, caring for the spiritual welfare and Baha'i education of the friends and children, etc., they and the friends themselves must at the same time be good citizens and loyal to the civil government...

order.why: Return to the vitality of community life as a measure.
Consider constructive contributions from enrolled and unenrolled participants.
shortened: On previous occasions we have explained that the maturity of a Spiritual Assembly cannot be assessed by the regularity of its meetings and the efficiency of its functioning alone. Rather its strength must be measured, to a large extent, by the vitality of the spiritual and social life of the community it serves--a growing community that welcomes the constructive contributions of both those who are formally enrolled and those who are not.

order.why: Read the full supplied Tablet on justice, dignity, and the interests of all.
Distinguish an institution’s duties from personal relationships.
Keep individual expression and humble consultation in view.
shortened: Let us also remember that at the very root of the Cause lies the principle of the undoubted right of the individual to self-expression, his freedom to declare his conscience and set forth his views.

Let us also bear in mind that the keynote of the Cause of God is not dictatorial authority but humble fellowship, not arbitrary power, but the spirit of frank and loving consultation. Nothing short of the spirit of a true Baha'i can hope to reconcile the principles of mercy and justice, of freedom and submission, of the sanctity of the right of the individual and of self-surrender, of vigilance, discretion and prudence on the one hand, and fellowship, candour, and courage on the other.

order.why: Consider confidence, obedience, and mutual cooperation.
Read the rejection of superiority and the call to consult with the friends.
shortened: Their functions is not to dictate, but to consult, and consult not only among themselves, but as much as possible with the friends whom they represent.

They should never be led to suppose that they are the central ornaments of the body of the Cause, intrinsically superior to others in capacity or merit, and sole promoters of its teachings and principles. They should approach their task with extreme humility, and endeavor by their open-mindedness, their high sense of justice and duty, their candour, their modesty, their entire devotion to the welfare and interest of the friends, the Cause, and humanity, to win not only the confidence and the genuine support and respect of those who they should serve, but also their esteem and real affection.

order.why: Join love with justice in resolving differences.
Consider the warning against dictatorial assertiveness.
Ask how over-administration can discourage a community.
Read the relation between firmness and humility in exercising authority.
Consider both social responsibility and freedom from being stifled.
Read the national institution’s coordinating and electoral purposes.
Examine how a national body can enable others to fulfill their tasks.
shortened: As to the National Assembly, whose inescapable responsibility is to guard the integrity, coordinate the activities, and stimulate the life, of the entire community, its chief concern at the present moment should be to anxiously deliberate on how best to enable both individual believers and local Assemblies to fulfil their respective tasks.

order.why: Consider qualifications alongside confidence in growth and assistance.
Conclude with capacity and service beyond gender and social standing.

questions: What would make humility and self-sacrifice visible in the way an assembly exercises authority?
How do practical responsibilities such as education and safeguarding funds express the spiritual purposes described here?
What can the variety of historical arrangements teach us about reading institutional guidance in context?
How might frank individual expression and wholehearted support for shared decisions strengthen one another?
What does comparison with the community’s response to neglected widows in Acts reveal about trustworthy service and the selection of those responsible for it?
How would you recognize an institution’s growing maturity in the daily life and capacity of the people it serves?

references.label: 1 · Acts 6:1–7 · Choosing people for neglected service
references.note: Read how a complaint about neglected widows leads the community to select people of good reputation, wisdom, and spiritual character for a practical responsibility. Compare the relationship between trust, selection, and care with the assembly readings. The account concerns a distinct apostolic community and does not establish the same institutional form.

subjects.displayTitle: Religious renewal: returning to a living source
subjects.introduction: Nobody tells the morning sun to go away because it shone yesterday, and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asks why religion should be treated differently. Every revelation is a springtime; every tree grown from the seed of reality bears fruit for a season and then ages, until the law of God is a name and the teachings an outward form. The grief at the centre of this teaching is the distance that opens between a founder and the people who carry his name: love turned to fanaticism, honey to poison, fellowship to war. Renewal is not rejection of what was given but return to it, a sapling of the same stock planted by the same Gardener. Jesus’ rebuke of a tradition that let a declared gift excuse the care of parents shows the same conflict between profession and practice. The road leads on into progressive revelation and the changing and unchanging parts of religion, into the misinterpretation of the Word of God, and into the violence in the name of God that renewal exists to end.
subjects.arc: Begin with the need for fresh light, follow the images of growth and decay, examine the distance between teachings and conduct, then explore recognition, changing conditions, and renewed fellowship.

order.why: Follow the seed, tree, fruit, and renewed planting.
shortened: From the seed of reality religion has grown into a tree which has put forth leaves and branches, blossoms and fruit. After a time this tree has fallen into a condition of decay. The leaves and blossoms have withered and perished; the tree has become stricken and fruitless. It is not reasonable that man should hold to the old tree, claiming that its life forces are undiminished, its fruit unequaled, its existence eternal. The seed of reality must be sown again in human hearts in order that a new tree may grow therefrom and new divine fruits refresh the world.

order.why: Open with the sun’s need to rise again today.
Meet the image of revelation as springtime.
Read renewal through a sapling of the same stock.
Consider outward forms as garments of a living reality.
Hear the seeker’s thirst amid competing claims.
Follow the thirsty seeker toward a sweet spring.
Ask why students dispute about teachers instead of learning.
Face the reversal from fellowship to violence.
shortened: All religions have created traditions that have no connection with the foundation of divine religion, and since these traditions differ, differences lead to disputation and disputation ends in warfare. The blood of the innocent is shed, possessions are pillaged and plundered, and children are left helpless and captive. Religion, which should be the cause of fellowship, becomes the cause of enmity. Religion, which should be as sweet honey, becomes deadly poison. Religion, which should be the cause of the illumination of the world of humanity, becomes the cause of darkness. Religion, which should be the cause of eternal life, has become the cause of death.

order.why: Read the lament over law used as a pretext for hatred.
Consider love displaced by fanaticism.
shortened: But today the first duties of religion are neglected. The first duty and the basis of each religion is the love of God. Love has vanished and hate and animosity have taken its place. Instead of these simple principles we now have dogmas and imitations, and because the dogmas and imitations differ we have constantly strife and war. Fanaticism is the only aim. These fanatics are actually thirsty for their brother's blood, they condemned one another and considered each other unclean.

order.why: Read the concise account of imitation leading to enmity.
shortened: The divine religions were revealed for love and amity and have brought out harmony among the different peoples and nations. But as time passed dogmas and imitations crept in and caused differences and enmity.

order.why: Keep the distinction between founders’ purposes and later imitation.
shortened: But alas! after their days certain dogmatic imitations crept in, and these imitations caused division. For the imitations which crept in were not reality but were purely superstitious and utterly inimical to the law laid down by the founders. They were distinct from the teachings given by the prophets because they were inimical; therefore they caused enmity and strife and division. In place of the unity which was intended to bind together the religionists, these imitations caused a regrettable separation. Instead of loving fellowship which was to animate then, the spirit of strife and discord animated them.

order.why: Read the criticism of outward observances that divide.
Read the reported argument of critics about followers’ conduct; the full source rejects their conclusion about the founders.
Keep the criticism of Italian aggression in its historical setting.
shortened: The Italians are a generous people, but they have become accustomed to the expression of generosity in words only, and therefore they have been guilty, in their aggressions upon the Turk, of conduct which is utterly atrocious and inexcusable, and such as no civilized nation should tolerate for a moment. This conduct would not have been possible if Italy lad lived the principles of the religion which has guided her for so many years. But, in her policies, this religion has never gone beyond the theatrical coloring of words.

order.why: Read the contrast between Christ’s counsel and warfare.
Consider self-interest changing the purpose of religion.
Retain the reported account of later doctrinal fabrication.
shortened: They were the Supreme teachers of monotheism like all the other prophets of God; but the succeeding generations misconstrued their words and in order to further their own selfish interests they fabricated these false doctrines.

order.why: Keep the reported account of priestly influence attributed.
Read the captivity image in its reported voice.
Hear the appeal to seek the light beyond self-seeking teachers.
Consider the damage to trustworthiness, friendship, and fidelity.
Read the denunciation of hatred and faithlessness in its particular setting.
shortened: O 'Ali! In the great city the fire of hatred, treachery, calumny, greed, tyranny and corruption blazeth bright. They have taken up faithlessness and cast away trustworthiness in opposition to God and His Cause. Thus have their heedless souls enticed them. They have broken God's Covenant and His Bond, and were not moved by God's counsel and His Word.

order.why: Set the commands against conflict beside the failure to heed them.
Keep the lament about religion’s loss of standing.
Read the reported account of dissatisfaction with religious teaching.
Keep the reported comparison with material philosophy attributed.
Read the account of government hostility and religious leadership’s failures.
Consider the relationship of ceremonies to knowledge and spiritual purpose.
shortened: Forms and rituals may be necessary to some people but the primary foundation of divine religion is the knowledge of the Almighty through scientific and reasonable proofs. Now we have forgotten this essential object and have clung to a set of dogmas and creeds which will not help us at all. These ceremonies are like unto the body and the spiritual Teachings like unto the spirit.

order.why: Read the inability of empty formalism to satisfy longing.
Keep the reported account of ceremonies displacing ideals.
Hear the call to uncover the image of truth.
Read the invitation to return to Christ’s teachings.
shortened: Discarding all the accumulated dogmas and pagan rituals of the past ages we must return to the fountain head of the Teachings of Christ as he uttered them here many generations ago. This is the only way.

order.why: Consider the renewal of the prophetic foundation through Baha’u’llah.
Read the reported image of an ancient path cleared of debris.
Keep the question about Baha’i teaching with its answer.
Distinguish clouds of imitation from fundamentals.
Calls for investigation beyond inherited dogmas and imitations.
Read the restored Q: and A: exchange with its visible source omission.
Consider the image of husks replacing the heart of the teachings.
Read the call for new illumination and thinking.
shortened: And since this is a luminous age and this century is the century of science, new teachings are necessary, a new illumination is essential, and a new life is required. Minds and souls will not accept old opinions - new thinking is needed and new teachings are necessary that are the spirit of this age and the light of this century.

order.why: Ask what remains of the original foundation in the source’s question.
Keep the broad criticism of Christian and Muslim practice attributed.
shortened: Regarding the matter that traces of these divine teachings existed in previous scriptures - those teachings were promoted and had their effect in their own time. Now they remain in the hands of nations like abrogated verses, having no authority whatsoever.
Observe the Christian nation - today no one acts according to Christ's counsels. Similarly look at Islam - they are entirely heedless of the divine counsels and admonitions in the Quran.

order.why: Consider the lamp whose wick remains after its light is gone.
shortened: But when those divine Teachings which pertain to the world of morals are forgotten, certain rules and customs arise in their place, proceeding from the world of self. Then that religion becomes the cause of abasement. Now the divine foundation has not remained. The lights of this lamp have set; only the wick and the candlestick remain, and from these no illumination is obtained.

order.why: Read sincerity and thirst for truth amid inherited traditions.
Examine the problem of distinguishing truth amid conflicting authorities.
Read the Iqan’s account of interpretation, leadership, and exhausted forms.
shortened: Such a condition as this is witnessed in this day when the reins of every community have fallen into the grasp of foolish leaders, who lead after their own whims and desire. On their tongue the mention of God hath become an empty name; in their midst His holy Word a dead letter.

It is unquestionable that in every succeeding Revelation the "sun" and "moon" of the teachings, laws, commandments, and prohibitions which have been established in the preceding Dispensation, and which have overshadowed the people of that age, become darkened, that is, are exhausted, and cease to exert their influence.

order.why: Consider inherited religious identity in the Bab’s challenging address.
Read the criticism of following others without investigation.
Keep the image of worship directed toward imagined idols.
Hear the reported call to release inherited burdens.
shortened: How long these withering customs, these stultifying rites! How long these blightening dogmas! How long these barren theological, hair-splitting, useless discussions. We must abandon entirely these things; we must free ourselves from these intolerable burdens; we must shake off our bodies this atrophy and this lethargy; we must come into full possession of all our god-given powers; we must soar toward the infinite altitude of divine Beauty; we must discard these fantastic traditions which have been handed to us as a precious heirlooms from ancestors and forefathers.

order.why: Keep the criticism of religious authorities in its own voice.
shortened: The primary cause and reason for the veiling of mankind have been, in the first instance, the divines, who in all ages and centuries have been the foremost cause of these mighty veils.

order.why: Join the lamp’s need for oil to the warning about veils.
Read the smoke and dust images in an address about opposition.
Consider expectation of divine days beside failure to recognize them.
shortened: Observe the religions of the world, how they remain veiled and debarred. Glory be to God! All await the divine days, and at all times they implore and supplicate with the utmost humility and devotion for the meeting with the Self-Sufficient, the Most High. Nevertheless, when the Sun of Truth shone forth from the horizon of the world, all remained occupied with their own idle fancies and devoted to the idols of their own selves. They have forsaken the Truth and clung to that which is unseemly.

order.why: Keep the related account of awaiting and turning away.
Read the particular appeal to a shaykh about expectation and denial.
Consider the contrast between calling for truth and rejecting its manifestation.
Keep the historical account of the promised Tree’s rejection.
Read the remembered denials of successive revelations.
shortened: When the Gospel was sent down they said: "This was not revealed from the Glorious One," and when Muhammad came with clear signs they said: "These are but fabrications."

order.why: Consider the suffering described as an effort to remove veils.
Read the address to the people of the Bayan in its historical setting.
Keep the polemical exchange about succession and its quoted opposing claim distinct.
Consider the warning about succession language becoming an obstacle.
Read the invitation to judge whether a statement comes from truth or desire.
Keep the rebuke addressed to the people of the Bayan.
Read the accusation of altering words and ordinances in its own terms.
shortened: Yet they were heedless and perverted the words of God from their places, and changed God's favor unto themselves, and altered what We had ordained for them to attain unto a station of mighty glory - to such extent that they ascend the pulpits and make mention of that which God hath not permitted them.

order.why: Read the call to receive the divine command.
shortened: Take what ye are bidden and abandon what the people possess, by the command of God, the Ordainer, the Ancient of Days.

order.why: Consider the warning about reliance on names and inherited tales.
Read the imagined regret about books and their Source.
Keep the broad statement about Iran attributed to the source.
Consider the image of losing the capacity to perceive fragrance.
Retain the account of changing Persian habits and the hope of renewal.
Keep the historical narrative of decline and renewed light in Iran attributed.
Read the reported criticism of Buddhist practice as a claim in this source.
Keep the reported judgments about Christian and Buddhist followers attributed.
Retain the reported account concerning Japan without presenting it as independently established history.
Keep the reported appeal concerning teachers in China in its setting.
shortened: China is in need of many good, Baha'i teachers - in order to unshackle their minds from the rusty chains of ancestral traditions.

order.why: Read the reported account of customs entering Christianity.
Consider the reported movement from symbols to literal interpretation.
shortened: Most of the churches used to worship idols. These introduced their idols into the new religion, the bells, candles, etc., in all about twenty one customs were in succession introduced. When they came to the Gospels they did the same. At first these innovations were employed only as symbols, but afterwards were interpreted literally - about 300 years after Christ.

order.why: Keep the severe historical judgments in the reported conversation attributed.
shortened: After my return to Alexandria, the Minister of the reception to the then Khedive invited me to his home where I found a number of Pashas and Beys with whom I spoke about religion and the need of reformation and urged the necessity of an entire rehabilitation of the moral codes referring to the Jews as an example of morbid tenacity to the ancient, putrid, antiquated laws of Mishna and a blind following of the Rabbis.

An old tree, whose very roots are dried up shall never again push forth leaves, blossoms and fruits. Will it ever become verdant by simply asserting that once I was a supple, young tree? Or a foolish dotard, will he ever become rejuvenated by claiming that once I was a strong, powerful athlete?

order.why: Read the explanation of baptism in relation to changing circumstances.
shortened: Consider, likewise, that in the days of John the Baptist the purification of baptism served to awaken and admonish the people and to cause them to repent of all sin and to await the advent of the Kingdom of Christ. But today in Asia, the Catholics and the Orthodox plunge infants into a mixture of water and olive oil, in such wise that some fall ill from this ordeal and tremble and struggle at the time of baptism. Elsewhere the priest sprinkles the baptismal water onto the forehead. But in neither case do these children experience any spiritual feelings. What good then can this do? Other peoples wonder and question why this infant is being plunged into the water, since it confers neither spiritual awareness nor faith nor awakening, but is merely a custom that is being followed.

order.why: Keep the interpretation of Revelation’s chronology in its scriptural context.
shortened: When, in the beginning of the seventh century of the Christian era, Jerusalem was conquered, the Holy of Holies--that is, the edifice that Solomon had erected--was outwardly preserved, but its outer court was seized and given over to the Gentiles.

"And the holy city shall they tread under foot forty and two months"; that is, the Gentiles will seize and subdue Jerusalem for forty-two months, or 1,260 days, or--each day being equivalent to a year--1,260 years, which is the duration of the Qur'anic Dispensation.

order.why: Read the reported interpretation of dry bones and renewed life.
Consider the garden’s need for continued care in the Cain and Abel interpretation.
shortened: In the spiritual significance, we find that Abel represents the Divine Law or Religion, and Cain the human nature. The Divine Law is present in man and attains a certain development when the human nature overcomes it. A man may take a forest and by skillful attention turn it into a garden. But if it be neglected for a time, it reverts into its former condition. So there is always present the tendency to nullify the action of the Divine Law or Religion.
A man may with the utmost care attend to a garden for a hundred years, but if it be neglected for a single year it will become a wilderness.

order.why: Read the full image of spiritual autumn and winter.
Follow the seasons from Christ’s springtime toward another renewal.
Keep the related reported account of the Mosaic cycle.
shortened: For instance, in the first beginning of the appearance of Moses was the sprint time of his day. The summer time was when many people had accepted him, believed in him, promulgated his teachings, that his fruit was gathered. Then came the autumn, when his commands first began to be neglected, and the true followers began to fall away, and the true teachings to sink into decay. Then came the winter, when the hearts ceased to turn unto God, where occupied with worldly things entirely, and spiritual death was apparent. Then came the spring time of Christ.

order.why: Consider the withering of the garden of hearts.
Read the return of spring after spiritual winter.
shortened: When the divine spring is over and the heavenly bounty ceases, the trees of being lie dormant. Lifelessness and stillness prevail over the world of man. People become spiritless and withered. Autumn and winter set in. There exists no flower or greenery, no cheerfulness or mirth, no happiness or joy.
Then the spiritual spring spreads its tent once more.

order.why: Keep the aging-tree analogy as the speaker’s argument.
Read the reported personification of religion as an aging figure.
shortened: Once upon a time religion was like a comely youth overflowing with vital force. The youth was in the utmost freshness and charm, adorned with infinite virtues and attuned with the music of vigor and health. But now he is stricken with old age. His eyes are dimmed, his ears do not hear, his feet are paralyzed, his hands are weak, his physical forces are exhausted. He is afflicted with senility and dotage.

order.why: Consider the rising luminary and tree imagery with the source’s omitted name visible.
Read the fresh flowers and daily food images.
Consider the continuing need for nourishment and the question about revelation’s end.
Read the divine dispensary analogy as spiritual teaching.
shortened: When a physical dispensary is closed, how greatly do people become alarmed. As soon as they learn of it, all people become distressed, wondering how they will cure their illnesses. The people's peace is entirely disrupted. They become severely anxious.
Yet if the divine dispensary is closed, due to their extreme heedlessness people express joy. What profound negligence this is.

order.why: Examine the rejection of the idea that divine grace is exhausted.
shortened: But some of the ignorant ones think that God's dispensation of Grace has come to an end, that His Treasury is exhausted, His Sovereignty terminated, His Spring of Bounties dried up. His creation concluded and the wheels of the chariot of His Everlasting Procession stopped! They believe that after the delightful spring of last year there will not be another joy-creating Spring.

order.why: Keep the reported contrast between transient sects and enduring verities.
shortened: Speaking about the various denominations and sects which now and then crop up amongst the various religions he said:

"They appear and disappear. They have no importance whatsoever in the religious world. They are not based upon a permanent foundation. They are built on the shifting sand of time. The essential verities of the divine religions are changeless. How many sects have sprang up again drowned by the sea of time! They are like unto bubbles which are and yet are not..."

order.why: Consider the distinction between essential constancy and manifested change.
Read renewal within one religion of God.
Keep the concise account of Christ renewing the ancient law.
Read the historical movement toward the Christian cycle.
shortened: Later they deviated from the straight path and turned away from the true way, falling again into their former degradation until the cycle of Christ came.

order.why: Consider the need for awakening when principles are neglected.
Keep the reported appeal for a fresh start.
Read each law’s completeness for its own time.
Consider changing secondary teachings in relation to human welfare.
Read the demands of a different age.
Consider the image of teachings that no longer heal every wound.
Read the stated need for changed laws and renewed reality.
Connect religious renewal with a world of new knowledge and practices.
Keep the reported parallel with renewed sciences, arts, and industries.
Consider the challenge to customs that obstruct moral development.
shortened: As everything evolves, so also does religion - as witness the doctrines that are losing their influence today. All religious rites and ceremonies, when adhered to, become the cause of destruction and struggle.

This is the day when dogmas must be sacrificed in our search for truth. We must leave behind all save what is necessary for the needs of today, nor attach ourselves to any form or ritual which is in opposition to moral evolution.

order.why: Read the reported warning about literal application across different settings.
Keep the reported recollection of the Bab changing sterile customs.
shortened: On that occasion, the blessed Person of `Abdu'l-Baha noted, "The ways of His Holiness the Bab in Bushihr caused many of the old and sterile traditions to be changed."

order.why: Consider the relationship of alteration to a new dawn.
Read renewed light following tyranny and loss.
Keep the description of virtues renewed with the dawn.
shortened: Similarly, today's relation to previous days is such that after darkness, selfish desires, unworthy deeds, and satanic acts had overtaken the world, and the merciful attributes and divine characteristics of the previous Manifestation were cut off and completely severed, then the true dawn broke and divine lights shone forth, and all these virtues were renewed on this day.

order.why: Read the reported hope for recognition through religion’s relation to present needs.
Consider materials gathered for the Temple of Humanity.
shortened: Now it is true that the present day religions are like unto dilapidated houses.
The religion of Baha'u'llah is preparing slowly yet assuredly, the materials out of which the Temple of Humanity shall be constructed.

order.why: Read the aim of restored honor and deliverance.
shortened: This Wronged One, from the earliest days until now, hath called aloud, with the most exalted summons, both kings and subjects, unto God---glorified be His majesty---seeking thereby but this: that lost honour be restored, and the abased and overturned standards, cast upon the dust, be uplifted once again.

Consider thou: with what power and ascendancy did the people of unity appear in the first days, and into what abasement and weakness are they now fallen! Whither hath that might departed, and from what source hath this feebleness arisen? No aim was intended save the exaltation of the Word of God---and, moreover, the deliverance of His servants.

order.why: Return to renewal as fellowship among different peoples.
Close the linked readings with concord and the unity of humanity.
Retain the supplied reflection on faithful practice and the need for reawakening.
Conclude with the supplied winter image and the question of what restores life.

questions: What do the images of sunrise, seasons, gardens, and nourishment reveal about the need for spiritual renewal?
How can a community distinguish a living tradition from a practice that obscures its original purpose?
What does the distance between founders’ teachings and followers’ conduct ask of someone evaluating a religion?
How might the critique of tradition in Mark’s account sharpen our attention to the actual effects of a religious practice?
How do these readings relate enduring spiritual principles to laws and forms suited to particular times?
What signs of fresh spiritual life would you look for in character, relationships, and shared action?

references.label: 1 · Mark 7:6–13 · When tradition frustrates care
references.note: Read Jesus’ criticism of a practice that allows a declared religious gift to excuse care for parents. Compare this concrete conflict between professed devotion and lived responsibility with the compilation’s concern about forms obscuring spiritual purpose. This particular Gospel dispute invites examination of practice; it does not by itself establish the Baha’i account of successive revelation.

subjects.displayTitle: Reading faithfully: words, meanings, and the reader’s desires
subjects.introduction: The trouble, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá told a visitor, is that you remember only what serves your purpose and forget the rest. Every reader of scripture knows the temptation, and the Bahá’í writings treat it as a spiritual danger rather than a scholarly lapse. Bahá’u’lláh explains that the corruption of a holy book rarely means its words have been erased; it means their meaning has been bent to fit idle fancy and desire, a single letter seized to prove a case while the Revealer of the whole is denied. Those who waited longest for the Messiah read their prophecies of iron rods and peaceable wolves so literally that they could not recognise Him when He came, and the pattern repeats whenever inherited explanations harden into a test that revelation itself must pass. The Qur’án’s distinction between clear verses and ambiguous ones, with its warning against pursuing interpretation to stir discord, sets the humility that faithful reading requires [1]. The question is finally one of conduct: does an interpretation yield truthfulness, justice and fellowship? The journey continues into the deliberate difficulty of the divine Word, the heedlessness that keeps familiar texts unread, and the renewal by which religion is corrupted and restored.
subjects.arc: Begin with selective memory and the consequences of a single word, distinguish textual alteration from distorted meaning, examine literal expectations and historical disputes, then return to faithful conduct and humility.

order.why: Distinguish perverting meaning from effacing actual words.
shortened: Nay, rather, by corruption of the text is meant that in which all Muslim divines are engaged today, that is the interpretation of God's holy Book in accordance with their idle imaginings and vain desires.

In yet another instance, He saith: "A part of them heard the Word of God, and then, after they had understood it, distorted it, and knew that they did so." This verse, too, doth indicate that the meaning of the Word of God hath been perverted, not that the actual words have been effaced.

order.why: Open with the danger of remembering only what serves one’s purpose.
Consider the consequences of misreading a single word.
shortened: Great error may result from the misinterpretation of a single word or expression of the sacred books.

order.why: Read the argument against dismissing the Gospel as wholly corrupted.
Consider the warning against altering evident meaning.
Read the charge to preserve the Word’s sanctity.
shortened: Corrupt not the holy, the all-embracing, and primal Word of God, and seek not to profane its sanctity or to debase its exalted character.

order.why: Examine the influence of desire and inherited theological limits.
Consider reciting scripture without grasping its intended meaning.
Read the distinction between long familiarity and understanding.
Keep the pointed criticism of reading without comprehension in its own voice.
Consider the use of an isolated word to support desire.
shortened: O people! Act in accordance with what ye have been commanded in the Tablets, and follow not the ways of the ignorant ones who have cast the ordinances of God behind their backs and followed the ways of the fabricators - they who have taken a word from the Book and interpreted it according to their desires. These, verily, are among the perverters.

order.why: Read the contrast between using verses and rejecting their Revealer.
Follow the extended historical argument about context, conjecture, and selective quotation.
shortened: Fie upon those who have turned away from all the signs, who have taken but a single letter from the Book and used it to prove their contentions, who have denied God through Whose command were sent down glorious scriptures and sublime tablets!

Beware, O people, lest ye pervert the words of God from their proper place. Bear witness to that which God hath witnessed, then be as brothers reclining upon couches face to face. Unite in such wise that no trace of discord may be detected among you. Through your unity will the Cause of God be made manifest throughout His creation, His tokens be established among His servants, and His light be proven throughout the worlds.

order.why: Distinguish original authorship from assembling borrowed phrases.
shortened: There are and there may be found some souls who collect the supplications of the Blessed Perfection and take out of every supplication a phrase or a sentence and then attribute it to themselves. Such people are like unto the man who gathers out of the Gospel sundry sayings of Christ, that is, he selects from every page a few words and as a result he composes phrases and sentences and claims to be the original writer.

order.why: Read the discussion of variant Qur’anic words in its particular controversy.
Consider outward wording and inner significance across scriptures.
Read the account of symbolic promises taken literally.
Keep the reported explanation of unfulfilled literal expectations attributed.
shortened: It is quite evident that the people did not understand the glad tidings, or prophecies, referring to the Christ in the Bible, for in the Old Testament they found this verse--that the coming one will come as a sovereign and will conquer the east as well as the west.
These people, finding these prophecies were not fulfilled in the time of Christ, nay rather (the reverse), reached to such a state that they even killed Him.

order.why: Read the signs of darkened sun and falling stars in the commentary’s setting.
Hear the quoted objections about the Qa’im as objections being examined.
Consider the criticism of exaggerated miracle stories in both Muslim and Christian accounts.
Read the visitor Mr. Reed’s question as a question, not a teaching attributed to Abdu’l-Baha.
Keep the reported manuscript argument as this source presents it.
Read the reported claim about inspired words and later human ideas attributed.
Keep the historical account of writings against Christ in the source’s voice.
Read the historical judgment about inherited traditions and Christ as an attributed claim.
Retain the reported statement about imagined worship in its historical setting.
Read the sequence of opposition to successive messengers.
Consider the remembered demands for outward signs.
Read the anecdote about speculative rankings and a scriptural reference.
Keep the account of expectations involving graves and trees in its particular polemical setting.
shortened: Among other things he asked about the sign of the Manifestation being that they would remove two well-known Shaykhs from their graves and hang them on two withered trees, whereupon those trees would instantly be observed to become green and flourishing. Observe how deluded this person is and at what station he stands. They carry their burdens upon their backs and perceive it not, and the volumes of allusions rest upon their hearts yet they understand not.

order.why: Read the criticism of beliefs about the Qa’im’s hidden life attributed.
Consider how an inherited belief becomes a test of others’ faith.
Read the account of breaking through inherited allusions.
shortened: Even as thou hast observed that after the widespread acceptance among all the servants of the Quranic references concerning the Promised Qa'im and His appearance in Jabulqa and Jabulsa, as well as the mention of the Seal of the Prophets which was the explicit text of the Book, God created servants who rent asunder all these references and evidences and the veil of clear text that was recorded in the Quran.

order.why: Keep the warning about interpretation through imagination.
shortened: But the heedless and ignorant souls have interpreted this word according to their own imaginings, and thus remained deprived of the living waters of certitude and forbidden from the manifestation of God.

order.why: Consider allusions becoming veils across religious communities.
Read the warning against being veiled by others’ words.
Read the contrast between inherited allusions and the encompassing Word.
Keep the images of familiar buzzing and unfamiliar birdsong.
Consider one veil being replaced by another.
Read the distinction between being reminded and perceiving.
shortened: We show them the horizon of certitude but they turn away from it, and We cause them to hear the cooing of the Dove but they hearken not. The Pen of Revelation remindeth them at all times but they remember not. They follow the ignorant and call them learned ones.

order.why: Keep the repeated appeal of the Pen.
Consider confidence in learning beside failure to understand.
Read the warning about knowledge becoming an obstacle.
Consider the drop-and-ocean and atom-and-sun analogies.
Hear the appeal to perceive the rising of inner meanings.
Read the flowing river and shining luminary as images of understanding.
shortened: The Tongue of God is speaking manifestly and evidently amidst the world, the Most Exalted Horizon is visible, the river of inner meanings is flowing from the Supreme Pen, and the Luminary of utterance is shining and gleaming from the highest horizon of contingent being. Nevertheless, all are heedless save a handful of the Letters of thy Lord's countenance - namely, those souls who have quaffed of the sealed wine by the name of the Self-Subsisting and have attained unto the Kawthar of the knowledge of the Beloved of all possibility.

order.why: Consider clear proofs and continued objection in the source’s account.
Read the Bayan’s stated relation to the promised revelation.
Consider the warning that the Bayan’s letters must not become a veil.
Read the account of the Bayan in relation to divine will.
Consider the Bab’s account of command, prohibition, and recognition.
shortened: Say: All this descendeth from a single Tree - God causeth to descend upon it as He pleaseth the exponents of His command and prohibition. Ye gaze toward your Lord. Consider whereby command is established and prohibition is established, that ye may not be veiled by them on the Day of Resurrection. For if God should will, He would make command into prohibition, even as ye now witness.

order.why: Read the distinction between desired worship and commanded worship, alongside counsel about differences.
Keep the Bab’s clarification of what he had commanded in the cited response.
shortened: And I bear witness before Thee concerning what people attribute to me, that I commanded naught in any book reaching unto all people save the purification of the air, and after making mention of the exaltation of Thy Cause and the Furqan, I joined therewith mention of the confirmation of Thy judgment from before upon all who believed in Thee until Thy judgment should reach them. And until that time I commanded no one with any new judgment from Thy presence, and in all wherein people differed they moved only in what pertained to the air.

order.why: Retain the historical letter’s denial of claimed authority in its own words and translation status.
Read the earlier letter’s distinctions between following signs and desires.
shortened: Those who followed Our signs aforetime -- these are the rightly guided. But those who have followed their vain desires -- naught of their deeds shall be accepted; these, indeed, are the lost.

order.why: Keep the Bab’s response to the charge of composing verses from Qur’anic letters.
shortened: As for the word of the idolaters concerning what We have revealed unto thee -- that the Remembrance taketh letters from the Qur'an and sendeth down verses in a clear Arabic tongue -- by thy Lord! They have lied against God and have fabricated concerning Our verses, prompted by what Satan cast into their souls.

And whoso saith that He hath taken letter by letter from the Qur'an -- such a one is indeed among the polytheists. The likeness of the creation of letters before God is as the likeness of your own creation. None can alter His signs; and on that Day the averse shall find for themselves, apart from the mention of the Name of God, neither witness nor helper.

order.why: Read the related rejection of that charge.
Consider the accusation of plagiarism and the response to it.
shortened: Among them is he who said that He hath plagiarized the verses of the Point and revealed them in His Name. At this My Most Exalted Pen hath lamented, and the dwellers of the Most Exalted Paradise. The Mother Book beareth witness to this in the most sublime station.

order.why: Keep the parallel account of the charge of stolen words.
Read the contrast between the Bab’s cited prayer and opponents’ actions.
shortened: O 'Ali-Akbar! Consider the station whereof the Primal Point hath spoken: "I seek refuge with Thee, O my God, lest my position on that Day be the position of the wicked." Observe what He said and what they say, what He did and what they do. They arose to cut down the Tree, and when their schemes were exposed, they opened their lips in calumny. You and all the people of the Bayan know that the Truth hath never been hidden nor concealed behind a veil.

order.why: Consider how counsels about recognition are said to have produced the opposite response.
shortened: The Point of the Bayan has said that in the year nineteen, all who are in the Bayan should write books to each other proving He Whom God shall make manifest. His purpose was that all should be occupied with this Most Great Remembrance through tongue, hand, pen and heart, lest the people of the Bayan should act like the Shi'ih sect. However, His counsels produced the opposite effect in most of the hearts of the opposers of the Bayan.

order.why: Keep the discussion of Mustaghath within its historical interpretation.
shortened: O My Name! All that was revealed in the Bayan concerning the mention of the Most Great Remembrance was revealed with utmost clarity. That which was made the cause of distinguishing the people and the degrees of recognition and the appearance of tests was the mention of Mustaghath, and now the meaning thereof hath been revealed from the Supreme Pen in the Clear Tablet - that which until now they have neither understood nor comprehended. The people are weak, and most have drunk the milk of vain imaginings from the breast of idle fancy.

order.why: Read the disputed calculation of the year Nine in its setting.
Consider the objection that revelation has appeared too soon.
Read the challenge concerning interpretation of the Bab’s declarations.
Consider names and offices becoming obstacles to meaning.
Keep the claim about a person’s stated rank in the source’s own words.
Read the criticism of measuring the promised station by imagined standards.
Retain the rejection of identifying the promised figure with the Primal Point Himself.
shortened: Those who have said that "He Whom God shall make manifest" is the Primal Point Himself have spoken unjustly.

order.why: Consider the claim that the whole Bayan points toward the speaker.
shortened: If they deny My mention, can any mention of them remain in the Bayan? Nay, by the Knower of hidden things! The entire Bayan is adorned with My Name and embellished with My mention.

order.why: Read the contrast between accepting earlier words and rejecting later revelation.
Keep the rebuke about failing to write and obey the Bayan.
Read the account of counsel, covenant, and denial.
shortened: There is no Tablet wherein We have not counseled the servants concerning this Announcement at which feet have slipped, and no Book wherein We have not commanded the people to be submissive before the Gate. The Names broke God's covenant and His testament until they openly denied the Mighty, the Unconstrained.

order.why: Read the objection that the Hidden Name ought not to appear.
shortened: Every misbeliever has taken for himself a vain fancy apart from God. They understand not. They worshipped the unseen throughout ages and centuries, yet when He manifested Himself they denied Him, saying: "It behooveth Him not to appear, for we have heard from our fathers that He is the Hidden Name." Say: By God! He is this One, and this is the treasured Mystery.

order.why: Consider attachment to names in place of their divine source.
Read the warning about repeating the conduct of a former community.
Keep the account of denying passages by alleging alteration.
shortened: Now the deniers among the people of the Bayan cling to the deeds of the past and utter the words of that party. They say the Bayan hath been altered, denying whatsoever hath been revealed concerning this Most Great Revelation and Most Great Announcement, attributing it to alteration, although this Cause is self-evident and needeth no mention, and all the books and scriptures of the world are dependent upon its acceptance.

order.why: Read the named controversy concerning the authenticity of the Text.
