shortened: O Abu'l-Qasim! The delusions of the previous party have emerged - the notorious Dawlat-Abadi has denied the Book of God and has intended to eliminate it. This grief is greater than all the griefs of the world. His followers say this Text is not authentic.

order.why: Consider the accusation of attempts to obliterate the Bayan and Qayyumu’l-Asma’.
shortened: In these days, sorrow upon sorrow and grief upon grief have appeared, for it hath been heard that an oppressor hath attempted to obliterate the Bayan and likewise the Qayyumu'l-Asma'. By His truth, this is an injustice whose fire consumeth the world and its peoples. Glory be to God! The words of the former party have resurfaced - they say "This Bayan is not that Bayan," just as they said "This Qur'an is not that Qur'an."

order.why: Read the reply to allegations that the Bayan was altered.
Keep the recurrence of the alteration claim in another address.
shortened: The words of the past have resurfaced - sometimes they say the Bayan has been altered, uttering calumnies the like of which have never been heard in creation.

order.why: Condemns distorting divine words while clinging to earlier scripture.
Retain the related polemical response in its own language.
Read the warning about an alleged intention to steal and erase the Book.
Keep the accusation of fabricated additions as an accusation in the source.
Read the account of removed Writings and the choice to remain silent.
Keep the reference to documentary evidence of falsification.
Read the account of a published declaration and later reconciliation.
shortened: Consider that Mirza Badi'u'llah wrote in his own hand, published and distributed that Mirza Muhammad-Ali had altered the Book of God, meaning he had removed passages from the Book of God and written other passages, attributing them to the Blessed Beauty. Yet despite this proclamation, he again formed bonds of friendship with him and made peace.

order.why: Consider the allegation of concealed efforts to sow doubt.
Keep the reported explanation of the Covenant’s purpose.
shortened: Some souls imagined that the Blessed Beauty had considerations of father and son, not knowing that He established the power of the Covenant for the propagation of God's Cause and the triumph of the Word of God.

order.why: Read the reported account of examining a purported Tablet.
shortened: "The House of Justice will put things right," He said. "It will gather together all the Sacred Writings, scrutinized them carefully, and pronounce its conclusive findings, and should any make contradictory remarks, he would be severely dealt with." Then He gave an explanation about how such a tablet never existed and was not from the Ancient Beauty and was not in His blessed idiom.

order.why: Distinguish the reported rumors from the teachings they purported to describe.
shortened: It was all based on false and ill-intended stories and rumors. For instance, it was voiced among people that this Person had made lawful that which was forbidden by God and made prohibited that which God had allowed, and that He had abandoned fasting, obligatory prayers, jihad, and discarded the religion of His Grandfather.

order.why: Keep the denunciation of false statements attributed to its source.
shortened: They who were not acquainted with so much as a letter of the Cause have risen to falsehood, speaking only as their own selves and desires have bidden them; and thereby are they accursed in this world and in the world to come, though they perceive it not.

order.why: Read the account of opposition and those who turned away from it.
Keep the accusation that veils of learning culminated in violence.
Read the account of the Bab’s martyrdom within the source’s denunciation.
Consider disagreement scattering the laws of wisdom and utterance.
Read the reported connection between misunderstanding and division.
Keep the distinction between imitation and religious reality.
Test interpretation against Christ’s command to sheathe the sword.
Read the related reminder of nonretaliation.
Consider justice as incompatible with quarrelling and fighting.
Read unity, morals, and benefit to humanity as clear purposes.
Consider the reported distinction between physical and spiritual destruction.
shortened: His intention is destruction, and it is divided into two parts, one physical and the other spiritual. The physical abomination of desolation is the razing and destroying of buildings. The spiritual abomination of desolation is the destruction of the teachings of GOD.

order.why: Keep the question about the golden calf in the reported narrative.
Read the deafness and mirror images in their particular account.
Consider the different effects attributed to receiving the same revelation.
shortened: One who has taste perceives the flavor of good fruits. For souls who are deprived of this station, the sending down of heavenly food has been and will be divine wrath.

Thus you witnessed how We seized the leader of the people with a wondrous Book, despite knowing his rejection and rebellion. Now what was a blessing for him became a curse, and its effects are evident in all lands.

order.why: Read the claim concerning worship and recognition in its theological setting.
Keep the warning about setting aside the Book.
shortened: They cast the Book of God behind their backs in that they followed every ignorant doubter.

order.why: Read the related contrast between the Book and imagination.
Retain the further statement of that warning.
Consider the seriousness attached to playing with verses.
shortened: Among the people are those who play with God's verses - for this do those in the heavens and earth curse them.

order.why: Read the counsel against unauthorized utterance.
Keep the warning against altering the Temple of God.
shortened: Beware lest ye alter the Temple of God. Know ye what We have informed you of before, then aid your Lord, the Mighty, the Wise.

order.why: Turn toward the invitation to radiant attention.
shortened: Cast ye aside all allusions and intimations, place them beneath your feet, and turn with radiant faces unto a station that hath been illumined by the lights of the Throne.

order.why: Read the Festival’s testimony and thanksgiving.
shortened: This is the Day whereon all things testified to that whereunto the Tongue of Power hath testified before the Divine Lote-Tree. All glory be to that which God hath bestowed upon us!

order.why: Close with a prayer for protection from distorted and self-serving interpretation.
shortened: O Lord! Protect Thy weak servants from the doubts of the people of vain desires, from the distortion of clear verses, from following ambiguous verses, and from the interpretations of the people of lusts.

questions: How might selective memory or a desire to confirm an existing belief influence the way we read a sacred text?
What differences do the passages draw between changing written words and distorting their meaning?
How can attention to metaphor and context coexist with respect for a text’s evident meaning?
What does the Qur’anic comparison invite us to consider about clear passages, ambiguity, and humility?
How does knowing who is speaking, to whom, and amid which dispute change the reading of these selections?
What habits of reading and discussion might help understanding lead to truthfulness, justice, and fellowship?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 3:7 · Clear and ambiguous verses
references.note: Read the distinction between clear or foundational verses and those described as ambiguous or allegorical, alongside the warning about pursuing interpretation to cause discord. Compare the humility of those grounded in knowledge with the compilation’s concern about desire and selective reading. The parallel translations offer an additional opportunity to examine how wording shapes understanding.
